questions.text:
Iron refining in New Zealand uses iron ore containing iron(III) oxide, Fe2O3. One step of the extraction involves the reaction of iron(III) oxide with carbon monoxide:

Fe2O3(s) + 3CO(g) -> 2Fe(l) + 3CO2(g)

The graph below shows the mass of iron(III) oxide, Fe2O3, as it reacts with 0.5 mol L-1 CO. The graph has two sections: Section A (steep decline) and Section B (curve levelling off).

Add a second line to the graph to predict the rate of decline in mass of iron(III) oxide if 2.0 mol L-1 CO were used instead.

Assume both reactions started with the same mass of ore.
questions.expectedAnswer: Added line should have a steeper gradient, and begin and end at the same mass of Fe2O3.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct second line (steeper gradient, same start and end mass).

questions.text:
With reference to the line you have drawn, explain the effect that this change in concentration of CO from 0.5 mol L-1 to 2.0 mol L-1 would have on the rate of this reaction.

In your answer you should include reference to:
- mass of Fe2O3
- each section of the line
- collision theory.
questions.expectedAnswer: The added line shows a steeper decline in mass of Fe2O3 due to the higher concentration of CO, meaning more frequent successful collisions.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: States that the same mass of Al2O3 is used OR correctly identifies that higher concentration increases rate. Merit: Correctly links increased concentration to increased frequency of successful collisions. Excellence: Full comparison including sections A and B.

questions.text: For the 0.5 mol L-1 NaOH solution used in another process, calculate the hydronium ion, H3O+, concentration.
Calculate the pH of the 0.5 mol L-1 NaOH solution.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Incorrectly calculates pH using [OH-]. Merit: Correct pH.

questions.text:
Using the principles of collision and particle theories, explain why using a catalyst would help to increase the rate of production of iron from iron(III) oxide.

You should include an energy profile diagram to support your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Basic definition of a catalyst. Merit: Links higher rate to lower activation energy. Excellence: Full explanation with energy profile diagram.

questions.text:
Ammonia for industrial use is manufactured in New Zealand using a reaction involving nitrogen, N2(g), hydrogen, H2(g), and ammonia, NH3(g), which is represented by the equilibrium constant expression below.

Kc = [NH3]^2 / ([N2][H2]^3)     Kc = 0.620 at 450 degrees C

Give the equation for this reaction.

The reaction is set up and allowed to reach equilibrium.

Calculate the concentration of nitrogen, N2, at equilibrium if the concentration of hydrogen, H2, is 0.250 mol L-1 and ammonia, NH3, is 0.500 mol L-1.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct substitution. Merit: Correct value.

questions.text:
The reaction is set up differently, with concentrations of each component as indicated below.

[NH3] = 0.520 mol L-1
[N2] = 0.700 mol L-1
[H2] = 0.620 mol L-1

Using a calculation, explain why this reaction is not at equilibrium.
questions.expectedAnswer:
Qc = [NH3]^2 / ([N2][H2]^3) = (0.520)^2 / ((0.700) x (0.620)^3) = 0.2704 / (0.700 x 0.2383) = 0.2704 / 0.1668 = 1.62
This value (1.62) is not equal to Kc (0.620), so the system is not at equilibrium. Since Qc > Kc, the reverse reaction will be favoured.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: States the calculated value is not the same as Kc. Merit: States the value is greater than Kc and therefore the reaction proceeds in reverse.

questions.text: Explain what must occur for the reaction to establish equilibrium.
questions.expectedAnswer: Since Qc > Kc, the reverse reaction must proceed at a greater rate than the forward, converting products back to reactants until Qc = Kc.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correctly identifies direction. Merit: States the reaction proceeds in reverse to establish Kc.

questions.text:
Ammonia, NH3, can be reacted with carbon dioxide to form urea:

2NH3(g) + CO2(g) <=> (NH2)2CO(s) + H2O(g)

Using equilibrium principles, identify, then describe, the effect on the position of the equilibrium when:

- ammonia, NH3(g), is added to the reaction mixture.

- sodium hydroxide, NaOH(aq), is added to the reaction mixture.
questions.expectedAnswer: Adding ammonia: forward reaction is favoured (an increase in a reactant shifts the equilibrium toward products). Adding NaOH: reverse reaction is favoured — NaOH reacts with the CO2 reactant (2NaOH + CO2 -> Na2CO3 + H2O), lowering [CO2], and the system responds by shifting backwards to replace the lost CO2.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: One correct answer. Merit: Correct answer linked to a reason. Excellence: Justification for both shifts.

questions.text:
This reaction can be performed under high pressure.

Explain why this is beneficial to the manufacturing process.
questions.expectedAnswer: Increasing the pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles. The forward reaction has 3 gas moles of reactant and 1 gas mole of product, so high pressure favours product formation.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies it will favour products. Merit: Explains increase favours side with fewer gas moles.

questions.text:
A reaction of H2PO4- is shown below:

H2PO4-(aq) + NH3(aq) <=> HPO42-(aq) + NH4+(aq)

Identify the species acting as an acid and the species acting as a base in the above equation, and their conjugate pairs.

Acid:                Conjugate base:
Base:                Conjugate acid:
questions.expectedAnswer: Acid: H2PO4-, Conjugate base: HPO42-. Base: NH3, Conjugate acid: NH4+.

questions.text: Write the equilibrium constant expression, Kc, for this process.

This reaction was initially performed at 25 degrees C to determine the Kc value. When the reaction temperature was increased to 50 degrees C, the Kc value decreased.

Explain whether the forward reaction is exothermic or endothermic.
questions.expectedAnswer: Decreasing Kc shows that increasing temperature favoured the reverse reaction. By Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature favours the endothermic direction. Since the reverse is favoured, the forward reaction must be exothermic.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises that the forward reaction is exothermic OR identifies that Kc decrease shows reverse favoured. Merit: Explains that the Kc decrease shows reverse was favoured when temperature increased AND explains that increasing temperature favours the endothermic reaction. Excellence: Exothermic nature of the forward reaction is justified linked to the decrease in Kc.

questions.text:
Solutions of 0.1 mol L-1 concentration were made of each of the following three substances:

C2H5NH2          HI          C2H5NH3Cl

Explain the pH of each of these solutions.

Include:
- a choice of pH value for each substance from the options below
- a classification for each substance
- any equations to explain the pH value.

pH options:    1-2    4-5    7    9-10    13-14
questions.expectedAnswer: C2H5NH2: pH 9-10 (weak base, partial proton acceptance). HI: pH 1-2 (strong acid, complete dissociation). C2H5NH3Cl: pH 4-5 (acidic salt).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies 2 correct pH values OR correctly classifies substances. Merit: Correct statement about the concentration of species linked to pH OR correct equations. Excellence: Full justification including correct equations for all three species.

questions.text:
Discuss the conductivity of the solutions:

C2H5NH2          HI          C2H5NH3Cl

Note they are all equal in concentration.

In your answer you should:
- explain the requirements for a solution to conduct electricity
- compare the extent of conductivity of each substance
- reference the relevant equations from your previous answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: HI is a strong acid, completely dissociating in water, producing a large number of freely moving ions, so it has the highest conductivity. C2H5NH3Cl is an ionic compound that fully dissociates into ions. C2H5NH2 is a weak base that only partially accepts protons, producing fewer ions.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct statement about free species. Merit: Correct statement of relative concentrations linked to conductivity. Excellence: Full justification including all three species.
